title: Tor bounds over a constant field sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme and let $\kappa$ be a field [def-weil-field]. On a small representative of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in a universe containing the site, let $\kappa_X$ be the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use the abelian category of $\kappa_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\kappa)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and the ordinary K-flat derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For every $B\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\kappa)$ and every pair of integers $a\le b$, the following are equivalent:
$$
H^i(B)=0\quad(i\notin[a,b]),\qquad
H^i(B\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\kappa_X}N)=0\quad(i\notin[a,b])\text{ for every }\kappa_X\text{-module sheaf }N.
$$
In the second condition $N$ is placed in degree zero. Equivalently, $B$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] exactly when its cohomology is concentrated in that interval. Thus finite Tor amplitude is equivalent to bounded cohomology. No constructibility, Noetherianity, finiteness of $\kappa$, or existence of enough points is assumed.

external.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat)

proof.text: Work on the chosen small pro-étale site, and write $R=\kappa_X$. Apply [lem-exc-constant-field-module-flat] to this topology and to the field $\kappa$: every sheaf of $R$-modules is flat for the ordinary sheafified tensor product. Its size and sheafification hypotheses are satisfied on the small representative in the enclosing coefficient universe; these are the usual ring and abelian-group sheafifications and their locally bijective equivalences, not an enough-points assumption. In particular every term of any complex of $R$-modules is flat.

source.place: Tags 03ER (definition-flat) and 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), specialized by the existing constant-field flatness node.

proof.text: Assume $H^i(B)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. The abelian-category bounded representative theorem [lem-sfb-bounded-representative] gives a cochain complex $P^\bullet$ and an isomorphism $B\cong Q(P^\bullet)$ with $P^i=0$ for $i<a$ and $i>b$. Now let $N$ be any $R$-module sheaf and regard $N[0]$ as a complex: its only possibly nonzero term is $N$ in degree $0$, flat by step 1, and its zero terms are flat because tensoring with $0$ gives $0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] with upper bound $0$: $N[0]$ is K-flat on this ringed site. The lemma applies to sites and independent coefficient universes; it does not require a topological-space presentation or stalks.

Fix $N$ as in step 2 and write $T_N(X)=\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes_R N[0])$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Since $N[0]$ is K-flat, [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent] says that $T_N$ sends every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $Q\circ T_N$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms and factors through the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] as $\overline T_N:D\to D$ with $\overline T_N\circ Q\cong Q\circ T_N$. Let $C^\bullet$ represent $B$ and let $q:P'\to C^\bullet$ be the K-flat resolution used in [def-weil-derived-tensor], so that $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N=Q\,T_N(P')$. Then $Q\,T_N(P')\cong Q\,T_N(C^\bullet)$ via $T_N(q)$, and $Q\,T_N(C^\bullet)\cong\overline T_N(QC^\bullet)\cong\overline T_N(QP^\bullet)\cong Q\,T_N(P^\bullet)$ via $QC^\bullet=B\cong QP^\bullet$ from step 2. In the total-complex formula for $T_N(P^\bullet)$, only the summand with second degree zero contributes, so degree $i$ is $P^i\otimes_R N$ and the differential is $d_P^i\otimes 1$. These terms are zero for $i\notin[a,b]$. Their kernels modulo images are therefore zero there, and by invariance of cohomology sheaves under isomorphisms in $D$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], $H^i(B\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RN)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$. Since $N$ was arbitrary, this proves the forward implication with the same endpoints.

source.place: Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism (tensor with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms), and the paragraph before definition-derived-tor (independence of the K-flat representative).

proof.text: Conversely, assume the tensor vanishing for every $N$. Represent the arbitrary object $B$ by a complex $C^\bullet$ and choose a K-flat quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; no bound on $B$ is used here. Set $N=R$, in degree zero. By [def-weil-derived-tensor] and [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R$ is represented by the complex with terms $P^i\otimes_R R$ and differential $d_P^i\otimes1$. Sectionwise the mutually inverse maps $p\otimes r\mapsto rp$ and $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ commute with restrictions and differentials. They give an isomorphism after sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], hence an isomorphism of this total complex with $P^\bullet$. Thus $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\cong B$. Cohomology is invariant under these derived isomorphisms [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], so the assumed vanishing for this particular $N$ gives $H^i(B)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude and the following paragraph testing with the coefficient sheaf.

proof.text: The second condition is exactly Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ by [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Taking existence of an ordered integer interval in the two implications identifies finite Tor amplitude with bounded cohomology. The zero object is covered by any ordered interval, including $[0,0]$. No constructibility or geometric finiteness condition entered any step.

No new nodes or Mathlib leaves. Checked the empty scheme, zero complex and singleton intervals without assuming enough points. Maintainer reader repair (2026-10-21): step 3 now derives the computation of $B\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ on the bounded representative from K-flatness of $N[0]$ and lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent, since step 2 gives only an isomorphism in $D$, not a resolution map of the representing complex.

tool_uses.why: General constant-field sheaf flatness supplies flat terms on any small ringed site, without enough points; the unit has no other such node.
General site-level bounded-above flat K-flatness makes N[0] K-flat for every module N over the constant field, without topological-space or stalk hypotheses.
General ringed-site K-flat resolution of an arbitrary representative is used to verify tensor with the coefficient unit in the converse before boundedness is known.

General ringed-site fact (Stacks 06YP) that tensoring with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms; it transports the derived tensor from the defining resolution to the bounded representative, which is only isomorphic to B in D. No node of the unit gives it.

Fixed: step 2 now shows N[0] is K-flat by lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat with bound 0 (N is flat by step 1). Step 3 cites lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent (Stacks 06YP), so Tot(−⊗N[0]) preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to D; this gives Q T_N(P')≅Q T_N(C)≅Q T_N(P), then the original degree count. proof_deps recomputed.
